Can cause fetal harm; use non-hormonal contraception
Do not breastfeed during and for 1 week after last dose
Effect of renal impairment on PK not studied

summary: Asparaginase Erwinia chrysanthemi (recombinant)-rywn (Rylaze) is an asparagine-specific enzyme used as part of a multi-agent chemotherapy regimen to treat acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and lymphoblastic lymphoma (LBL) in adult and pediatric patients 1 month or older who have developed hypersensitivity to E. coli-derived asparaginase. It is given intramuscularly, with premedication to reduce hypersensitivity. Key safety signals are serious hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis, pancreatitis, thrombosis and hemorrhage (coagulopathy), and hepatotoxicity including veno-occlusive disease - all of which require monitoring and can be life-threatening.
indications: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) as a component of a multi-agent chemotherapeutic regimen, in adult and pediatric patients 1 month or older who have developed hypersensitivity to E. coli-derived asparaginase

Lymphoblastic lymphoma (LBL) as a component of a multi-agent chemotherapeutic regimen, in adult and pediatric patients 1 month or older who have developed hypersensitivity to E. coli-derived asparaginase

dosage.n: Replace one calaspargase pegol dose with 11 doses, or one pegaspargase dose with 7 doses

dosage.d: 25 mg/m2 Monday morning and Wednesday morning; 50 mg/m2 Friday afternoon
dosage.t: Mon/Wed AM and Fri PM (Fri dose 53-58 h after Wed dose)
dosage.n: Replace one calaspargase pegol dose with 9 doses, or one pegaspargase dose with 6 doses

dosage.d: Hold; resume when amylase/lipase <1.5x ULN and symptoms resolved
dosage.n: Permanently discontinue if necrotizing or hemorrhagic pancreatitis is confirmed
If total bilirubin >10x ULN, discontinue and do not make up missed doses

dosage.d: Grade 3-4 hypersensitivity: discontinue permanently; severe/life-threatening thrombosis: discontinue; Grade 3-4 hemorrhage: hold and evaluate coagulopathy
dosage.n: Uncomplicated thrombosis: hold, treat with antithrombotic therapy, then consider resuming with continued anticoagulation

admin: Premedicate 30-60 minutes before each dose with acetaminophen, an H1 blocker (e.g., diphenhydramine) and an H2 blocker (e.g., famotidine) to reduce hypersensitivity
Ensure resuscitation equipment and agents to treat anaphylaxis (epinephrine, oxygen, IV steroids, antihistamines) are available before administering
Administer by intramuscular injection only; the intravenous route is not approved
Inspect for particulates, cloudiness or discoloration and discard the vial if present; do not shake the vial
Limit volume per injection site to 2 mL; if greater, split equally into multiple syringes/sites and rotate sites
Do not inject into scar tissue or areas that are reddened, inflamed or swollen; discard unused drug in single-dose vials
If not used immediately, store the prepared syringe(s) at room temperature (15-25 C) up to 8 hours or refrigerated (2-8 C) up to 24 hours
moa: Asparaginase Erwinia chrysanthemi (recombinant)-rywn is an enzyme that catalyzes conversion of the amino acid L-asparagine into aspartic acid and ammonia. Depletion of plasma asparagine kills leukemic cells, which have low asparagine synthetase expression and therefore depend on an exogenous source of asparagine for survival; normal cells can synthesize their own asparagine.

absolute: History of serious hypersensitivity reactions to Erwinia asparaginase, including anaphylaxis
History of serious pancreatitis during previous asparaginase therapy
History of serious thrombosis during previous asparaginase therapy
History of serious hemorrhagic events during previous asparaginase therapy
relative: Prior hypersensitivity to other asparaginase products
monitor: Signs/symptoms of hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis with each dose
Amylase, lipase and symptoms of pancreatitis
Signs of thrombosis (e.g., sagittal sinus thrombosis, pulmonary embolism) and hemorrhage
Bilirubin and transaminases for hepatotoxicity and veno-occlusive disease

preg: Based on animal reproduction studies, asparaginase Erwinia chrysanthemi can cause fetal harm, with structural abnormalities and embryo-fetal mortality observed at exposures below the recommended human dose. There are no adequate human data. Verify pregnancy status before initiating, advise pregnant women of the risk, and advise females of reproductive potential to use effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on the presence of asparaginase Erwinia chrysanthemi in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
renal: The effect of renal impairment on the pharmacokinetics of asparaginase Erwinia chrysanthemi has not been studied; no dose adjustment is specified.
hepatic: Asparaginase is contraindicated in patients with severe hepatic impairment. Hepatotoxicity, including severe, life-threatening and potentially fatal hepatic veno-occlusive disease, has been observed; evaluate bilirubin and transaminases before each cycle and at least weekly during treatment through 4 weeks after the last dose, and hold or discontinue per the degree of bilirubin elevation.

major: Concomitant hepatotoxic agents or anthracycline-based multi-agent chemotherapy - additive risk of hepatotoxicity and veno-occlusive disease
moderate: Anticoagulants/antiplatelet agents - asparaginase-induced coagulopathy may increase bleeding or unpredictable clotting
Drugs that increase pancreatitis risk - additive pancreatic toxicity
minor: No formal drug interaction studies have been conducted with this product
interactions.food: Not applicable - administered by intramuscular injection.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; avoiding alcohol is prudent given hepatotoxicity risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes elevated bilirubin/transaminases, amylase/lipase, hyperglycemia, decreased fibrinogen and antithrombin III, and prolonged aPTT; serum asparaginase activity (SAA) may be monitored to confirm adequate asparagine depletion.

serious: Febrile neutropenia and serious infection (including fatal infection)
rare: Acute respiratory distress syndrome, pulmonary edema
emergency: Severe or life-threatening thrombosis (e.g., sagittal sinus thrombosis, pulmonary embolism)
Hepatic veno-occlusive disease / acute liver failure

monitoring: Monitor closely for hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis during and after each injection; ensure resuscitation readiness
Bilirubin, transaminases, glucose and clinical exam before treatment, every 2-3 weeks, and at least weekly during cycles through 4 weeks after the last dose
Amylase and lipase plus symptoms (severe abdominal pain) for pancreatitis
Signs of thrombosis (headache, limb swelling, dyspnea, chest pain) and of hemorrhage (unusual bleeding/bruising)
Coagulation parameters (PT, PTT, fibrinogen, antithrombin III) when bleeding or clotting is suspected
Signs of hepatic VOD - rapid weight gain, fluid retention/ascites, painful hepatomegaly, rising bilirubin
counsel: Seek medical help immediately for signs of allergic reaction - rash, swelling of lips/face, difficulty breathing, dizziness
Report severe abdominal pain that may signal pancreatitis
Report headache, arm or leg swelling, shortness of breath, or chest pain (possible blood clot)
Report any unusual bleeding or bruising to your healthcare provider
Report yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe nausea/vomiting, or easy bruising (possible liver problems)
Use effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose; do not breastfeed during and for 1 week after treatment
pk: Asparagine depletion follows dosing; median Tmax ~12 h after IM injection
Tmax 12 h (range 8-24 h); Cmax ~2.3-4.1 U/mL serum asparaginase activity
Maintains nadir serum asparaginase activity across the 48 h or Mon/Wed/Fri dosing interval
Store refrigerated at 2-8 C (36-46 F) in original carton, protected from light; do not shake or freeze
pearls: Indicated specifically for patients who have developed hypersensitivity to E. coli-derived asparaginase - it provides an Erwinia-derived alternative
Always premedicate (acetaminophen + H1 + H2 blocker) and have anaphylaxis treatment immediately available - anaphylaxis occurred in ~2% of patients
Approved for intramuscular use only; the intravenous route is NOT approved and was associated with more hypersensitivity
Four enzyme-specific toxicities to watch: pancreatitis, thrombosis, hemorrhage (coagulopathy), and hepatotoxicity including VOD
Two interchangeable schedules replace one long-acting asparaginase dose - 11 (q48h) or 9 (M/W/F) doses for calaspargase pegol, 7 or 6 doses for pegaspargase
Hold for lipase/amylase >2x ULN or symptomatic pancreatitis; discontinue permanently if necrotizing/hemorrhagic pancreatitis confirmed
Serum asparaginase activity can be used to confirm adequate asparagine depletion
missed: If a dose is missed, do not double up. For hepatotoxicity requiring discontinuation at total bilirubin >10x ULN, do not make up missed doses. Otherwise, follow the prescriber's instructions to resume the scheduled regimen; the Friday afternoon dose should be given 53-58 hours after the Wednesday morning dose on the M/W/F schedule.
overdose: No specific overdose data or antidote is described. Management is supportive, with monitoring and treatment of hypersensitivity, pancreatitis, coagulopathy/bleeding, thrombosis and hepatotoxicity as they arise.
